rain_note: Torrential rains in the first and second weeks of September 2015; no amounts reported
summary: Torrential rain in the first half of September 2015 reportedly caused flood damage in and around Freetown before the major 16 September flood; exact days, places and impacts were not found and the reports may partly overlap the 16 September event.
evidence: Torrential rains in the first and second weeks of September 2015 caused extensive damage in and around Freetown, Sierra Leone, largely due to rivers bursting their banks.

rain_note: Continuous heavy rain over the preceding couple of days; one report describes a six-hour torrential downpour on 16 Sept; no amounts reported
summary: Torrential rain on Wednesday 16 Sept 2015 flooded low-lying settlements across Freetown; reported deaths ranged from 4 (State House) to 12 (VOA), with 10 the figure most often cited later; 12,000-14,000 people were affected and about 3,000 sheltered in the National (Siaka Stevens) and Attouga stadiums; the government ordered people to stay home on 17 Sept.
evidence: At least four people were killed and scores injured following torrential rains in Sierra Leone's capital on Wednesday (Reuters); later summaries: 14,000 people affected and 10 reported dead.

time_of_day: early morning (Regent/Sugar Loaf slope collapse reported at about 05:45); heavy rain on 13-14 Aug
rain_note: Three days of torrential rain beforehand; about 1,040 mm in Freetown from 1 Jul to 14 Aug (about 3x normal); >100 mm in the 7 days to 12 Aug (Weather Underground); one study cites three consecutive days with 126 mm, 10-14 Aug
summary: After three days of torrential rain, part of Sugar Loaf mountain collapsed above Regent in the early morning, sending a debris flow about 6 km down the Babadorie/Juba river valley to Lumley while flash floods hit other parts of Freetown; about 500 bodies were confirmed and 1,141 dead or missing is the most-cited total, with more than 3,000 left homeless (landslide plus floods).
evidence: Sugar Loaf mountain partially collapsed, triggering mudslides in the early morning of August 14, which damaged or completely submerged several houses and structures; at least 3,000 people are homeless and over 300 houses have been destroyed.

rain_note: Extremely heavy rain over central and western Freetown that night; no amount reported
summary: New overnight flooding in downtown Freetown, 12 days after the Regent disaster, flooded the Kroo Bay health centre, bridge and school; 1 person died and 2 were injured.
evidence: New flooding appeared on the night between Saturday and Sunday 26/27 August in downtown Freetown, and has flooded a health centre, the bridge and a school at Kroo Bay. One person is reported dead and two injured.

time_of_day: overnight: heavy continuous rain from about 22:00 on 1 Aug until the morning of Friday 2 Aug
rain_note: Heavy continuous downpour from 22:00 on 1 Aug to the next morning; came after persistent torrential rains since late May 2019 on saturated soil; no amounts reported
summary: Overnight torrential rain caused flash floods and landslides across Freetown and Western Rural: 7 bodies were confirmed (1 Kroo Bay, 2 Culvert, 3 Bathurst after a wall fell on a house), the perimeter wall of the Queen Elizabeth II Quay was breached and people were trapped in Blackhall, Kissy; ONS counted 985 households completely damaged and 5,381 people homeless (5,000-8,000 displaced in other estimates).
evidence: At least seven people are dead after flash flooding hit Freetown on Friday 2nd August, 2019 amid torrential rains, mortuary sources said.

summary: A second flood hit 14 Freetown communities (not named) in the early hours of 15 Aug 2019; a quick assessment found 200 more households affected, almost a third of them completely destroyed.
evidence: in the early hours of August 15th, more flooding was reported in 14 communities in Freetown, and 200 more households were affected, with almost one-third of these completely destroyed.
